target_customer: Data and business teams at companies with a data warehouse such as Snowflake or BigQuery
problem: Business users depend on analysts and dashboards to answer data questions, and trusted answers take too long.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription (a directory lists 180 per month billed annually)
product_category: AI data analyst (chat over a data warehouse)

founders.name: Theo Tortorici
founders.background_notes: YC page lists three founders and gives no bios for him.

founders.name: Rick Radewagen
founders.background_notes: YC bio: analyst in a world of data; creator of well-arranged pixels. He authored the YC launch post.

founders.name: Sven Rudolph
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on YC and EveryDev.

technical_complexity.rationale: Early on, the team built a Snowflake data catalog; the later LLM product needs reliable SQL generation and governance, which became tractable with language models after 2022.

defensibility.rationale: Learned metric definitions and integrations create some lock-in, but many AI analyst tools can be built on the same models.

market_need_then: The YC launch post contrasts Dot with searching through dashboards and says trustworthy data plus correct logic is needed for analytics; no dated demand numbers were found.

branding.domain_note: Uses getdot.ai, a prefix and the AI TLD, rather than dot.com.

identity.mascot_or_character: A fox mascot appears on the company site
identity.voice_and_tone: Short, approachable; tagline Be smarter, faster

rebrands.why: The team moved from a Snowflake data governance tool to an AI analyst; whether it was a rename or a new product is not stated in the sources opened

brand_strength.rationale: A branding search found nothing about the name or mascot origin. Only the site shows the fox mascot and tagline.

pivots.from: Sled, a data catalog and governance tool for Snowflake
pivots.to: Dot, an AI data analyst you chat with
pivots.why: The YC launch post says the Sled work taught the team the importance of trustworthy data combined with correct logic; the post is undated but says it was over three years ago

outcome_analysis: Dot, built by Snowboard Software GmbH, shifted from the Snowflake data catalog Sled to an LLM based data analyst and now lists customers including Duolingo, Airbyte and BlaBlaCar plus SOC 2 Type II on its site. Funding is not publicly confirmed, so the story is a small, active team that rode the language model wave.
notes: Funding: EveryDev lists 125K raised (an estimate), PitchBook snippet 125K and another source 500K, all unverified, so no round is recorded. EveryDev names Sven Rudolph as founder and Theo Tortorici as co-founder and managing director and omits Radewagen, while the YC page lists all three. Competitor search returned PitchBook names such as Atlan and Collibra for the earlier Sled product without dates, and the YC launch post names no rivals, so the list is empty. Company site gives legal entity Snowboard Software GmbH.
